common_name: Mountain Heartleaf (Southern Appalachian Evergreen Wild Ginger)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in fall or early spring into rich, humus-laden, consistently moist woodland soil in deep shade; this slow-spreading rhizomatous species resents root disturbance once established, so site it where it can remain undisturbed for years.

directions: Mountain heartleaf is a southern Appalachian endemic in the wild-ginger family, named for its leaf base, which narrows or contracts into the petiole rather than forming the deep heart-shaped notch typical of most related Hexastylis species. Like its relatives it carries leathery, evergreen, mottled leaves that form a low, slowly spreading groundcover, while the jug-shaped maroon-brown flowers are borne at ground level beneath the foliage in spring, largely hidden from view and pollinated by small flies. It is found in rich cove forests and wooded slopes of the Carolina and Georgia Piedmont-to-mountain transition zone, generally on moist, humus-rich soils. Give it the same deep shade and steady moisture as other native Hexastylis species, and avoid disturbing the shallow rhizomes once a clump is established.
